quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When riding with a group of motorcyclists, a staggered formation:

options.text: Should not be used when entering or exiting a highway.
Should be used when riding in curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used when entering or exiting a highway.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually good. But switch to single-file when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: The key to making a quick turn is to:

options.text: Get your motorcycle to lean quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get your motorcycle to lean quickly.
questions.explanation: To turn quickly, lean your motorcycle in the direction you want to go. The sharper the turn, the more the bike must lean.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: For motorcycle operators, eye protection is:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle operators must wear proper eye protection when riding.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the motorcyclist's following distance should:

options.text: Be the same as it normally would be.

questions.explanation: A motorcycle towing a trailer needs more following distance. The extra weight means the motorcycle takes longer to stop.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should always position your motorcycle:

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
In a position that allows you to most effectively see and be seen.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a position that allows you to most effectively see and be seen.
questions.explanation: Position your motorcycle to see oncoming traffic and be seen by others. On a left curve, stay right to spot oncoming cars. On a right curve, stay left and away from the centerline.

questions.question: When taking a curve while riding in a group, you should be in:
questions.explanation: Groups usually ride in staggered formation. Switch to single-file when taking curves, making turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: The front and rear brakes need to be used at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
Use the front brake to increase stability of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn. It can cause the bike to tip. Use only the rear brake to control your speed.

questions.question: Of the following, it is most important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: Someone is following you too closely.
There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.explanation: Flash your brake light when slowing or stopping suddenly. Motorcycle brake lights are not as noticeable as car brake lights. This warning helps others see you are slowing down.

questions.question: If you have a passenger aboard your motorcycle, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride at speeds that are slower than usual.
Allow more distance to stop than usual.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: With a passenger, ride slower and allow more stopping distance. The passenger should hold the passenger handgrips or hold the operator's waist, hips, or midsection firmly.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials when riding, even during daytime hours.

questions.question: How should you control a motorcycle?

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up
Press your knees against the fuel tank
Sit so your arms are straight when holding the handlebars

questions.correctAnswerText: Press your knees against the fuel tank
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your elbows should bend slightly when holding the handlebars. Press your knees against the fuel tank to help keep your balance.

questions.question: How should you swerve correctly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn
questions.explanation: To swerve away from danger, push lightly on the handgrip on the side where you want to go.

questions.question: What blood alcohol content (BAC) level makes a person legally intoxicated?
questions.explanation: A person is legally intoxicated at 0.08 percent BAC or higher. It is illegal and unsafe to drive a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle provides the most stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's stopping power. Use both front and rear brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider NOT do when approaching an intersection?

options.text: Choose a lane position to be more visible
Cover the clutch and brakes to be ready to stop

questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that makes you visible to other drivers. Cover your clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time. Slow down when approaching an intersection. Do not change speed or position suddenly, as this may confuse other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind intersection?

options.text: Move to the part of your lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible
Stop at the sign and then proceed normally
Flash your lights and honk to warn other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of your lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible
questions.explanation: Move to the part of your lane that puts you in other drivers' line of sight as quickly as possible.

questions.question: What should you do when riding over rough pavement in a construction zone?

options.text: Look down at the road surface
Keep your head and eyes up
Stay on the left side of your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding over rough pavement in a work zone. Ride slowly, keep steady throttle control, and do not fight with the handlebars.

questions.question: What should you do when passing another vehicle?

options.text: Exceed the speed limit by no more than 10 mph to complete the pass
Pass more than one vehicle at a time

questions.explanation: Complete all passes while staying within legal speed limits. Pass only when it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What is the best position to ride in within a lane?
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position for all situations. Good riders change their position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When turning, what should you do?

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head to look through the turn. Keep your shoulders still.
Turn your head and shoulders together to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head to look through the turn. Keep your shoulders still.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon. Turning your shoulders may cause you to steer off course.

questions.question: If you are passing another vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: You may drive faster than the speed limit until the pass is complete.
You may ignore no passing zone markings if you started the pass in a passing zone.
You must follow the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must be completed within the posted speed limits. Passing is only allowed in areas marked for passing.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, where should you ride in your lane?
questions.explanation: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
Stop only if you need to yield to other traffic.
Other vehicles will enter the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely. Yield to all crossing traffic and pedestrians. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, where should you ride in your lane?
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. This is the safest position. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle increases the risk of a collision. Riding on the far side can cause the driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns of a divided roadway ahead.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You will have time to react to hazards.
You will have space to maneuver.
You will have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you react to hazards and maneuver safely. This space does not help you accelerate faster when entering a curve.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that traffic ahead will merge.

questions.question: Lane lines that separate traffic moving in the same direction are what color?
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is displayed on the back of slow-moving vehicles. These vehicles move slower than 25 mph. Examples include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.
